title: Auto Keyword
description: Deduce type automatically using auto keyword (C++11)
explanation: Auto deduces the type from the initializer at compile time.

title: Auto With Reference
description: Use auto with reference qualifiers
explanation: Auto& deduces lvalue reference, auto&& deduces forwarding reference.

title: Decltype
description: Query the type of an expression (C++11)
explanation: Decltype returns the type of an expression without evaluating it.

title: Trailing Return Type
description: Specify return type after parameters using auto and ->
explanation: Trailing return types are especially useful with templates and decltype.

title: Nullptr
description: Use nullptr instead of NULL or 0 for pointers (C++11)
explanation: Nullptr is type-safe and avoids integer-pointer ambiguity.

title: Constexpr Function
description: Evaluate function at compile time (C++11)
explanation: Constexpr allows compile-time evaluation when inputs are known at compile time.

title: Constexpr Variable
description: Declare compile-time constant variable (C++11)
code:
constexpr int MAX_SIZE = 1000;
constexpr double PI = 3.1415926535;
explanation: Constexpr variables are evaluated at compile time.

title: Consteval (C++20)
description: Force compile-time evaluation (C++20)
explanation: Consteval functions must produce a constant; they cannot be called at runtime.

title: Constinit (C++20)
description: Guarantee constant initialization for static variables (C++20)
code:
constinit int global = 42;
constinit static int counter = 0;
explanation: Constinit ensures a variable has static initialization, avoiding dynamic init order fiasco.

title: Enum Class Scoped Enum
description: Declare strongly typed scoped enumeration (C++11)
explanation: Scoped enums don't leak names and don't implicitly convert to integers.

title: Enum Class With Underlying Type
description: Specify underlying type for scoped enum (C++11)
explanation: You can control the underlying integer type of an enum class.

title: Override Specifier
description: Mark a virtual function override explicitly (C++11)
explanation: Override lets the compiler check that the function actually overrides a base class method.

title: Final Specifier Class
description: Prevent a class from being inherited (C++11)
explanation: A final class cannot be used as a base class.

title: Final Specifier Method
description: Prevent further overriding of a virtual function (C++11)
explanation: Derived classes cannot override a final virtual function.

title: Defaulted Function
description: Explicitly request default compiler-generated function (C++11)
explanation: Default tells the compiler to generate the default implementation.

title: Deleted Function
description: Prevent use of a special member function (C++11)
explanation: Deleted functions cannot be called, useful to disable copy semantics.

title: Lambda Basic
description: Basic anonymous lambda function (C++11)
explanation: Lambda creates a callable function object inline.

title: Lambda With Parameters
description: Lambda function with parameters (C++11)
explanation: Lambdas can take parameters like regular functions.

title: Lambda Capture By Value
description: Capture external variables by value (C++11)
explanation: The lambda captures a copy of x at the point of definition.

title: Lambda Capture By Reference
description: Capture external variables by reference (C++11)
explanation: The lambda can modify the captured variable since it captures by reference.

title: Lambda Default Capture All By Value
description: Capture all external variables by value (C++11)
explanation: [=] captures every automatic variable used in the lambda by value.

title: Lambda Default Capture All By Reference
description: Capture all external variables by reference (C++11)
explanation: [&] captures every automatic variable by reference.

title: Mutable Lambda
description: Allow modification of captured-by-value variables in lambda (C++11)
explanation: Mutable allows the lambda to modify its copy of captured-by-value variables.

title: Generic Lambda (C++14)
description: Lambda with auto parameters for generic behavior (C++14)
explanation: Generic lambdas use auto parameters, creating a function template.

title: Lambda Initializer Capture (C++14)
description: Capture with an initializer expression (C++14)
explanation: Init capture enables move-only types to be captured and custom initialization.

title: Constexpr Lambda (C++17)
description: Lambda that can be evaluated at compile time (C++17)
explanation: Lambdas are implicitly constexpr if possible since C++17.

title: String View Declaration (C++17)
description: Create a non-owning view of a string (C++17)
explanation: String_view is a lightweight, non-owning reference to a string.

title: String View Parameters
description: Use string_view as function parameter for efficiency (C++17)
explanation: String_view avoids copying when passing string arguments, works with both string and char*.

title: String View Substr
description: Extract substring from string_view without copying (C++17)
explanation: String_view::substr returns another string_view, no allocation occurs.

title: Optional Declaration (C++17)
description: Represent an optional (nullable) value (C++17)
explanation: Optional holds a value or nothing, useful for functions that may fail.

title: Optional Has Value And Access
description: Check and access optional value (C++17)
explanation: has_value() checks if optional contains a value, value() returns it.

title: Optional Value Or
description: Get optional value or a default (C++17)
code:
optional<int> opt;
cout << opt.value_or(0); // prints 0
explanation: value_or returns the contained value or a fallback if empty.

title: Optional Return From Function
description: Return optional from a function to indicate possible failure (C++17)
explanation: Return nullopt to indicate failure, or the value on success.

title: Variant Declaration (C++17)
description: Type-safe union that can hold one of several types (C++17)
explanation: Variant holds exactly one value of the specified types at any time.

title: Variant Visit
description: Apply a visitor to the currently held variant value (C++17)
explanation: Visit calls the appropriate lambda overload based on the active variant type.

title: Variant Holds Alternative
description: Check which type a variant currently holds (C++17)
explanation: holds_alternative<T> checks if the variant currently holds type T.

title: Variant Get If
description: Safely access variant value with get_if (C++17)
explanation: get_if returns a pointer to the value if it matches the type, or nullptr otherwise.

title: Any Declaration (C++17)
description: Hold a value of any type using type erasure (C++17)
explanation: Any can hold a value of any copy-constructible type.

title: Any Cast
description: Retrieve value from std::any using any_cast (C++17)
explanation: any_cast throws bad_any_cast if the requested type doesn't match.

title: Span Declaration (C++20)
description: Non-owning view over a contiguous sequence of objects (C++20)
explanation: Span is a lightweight reference to a contiguous array, like string_view for arrays.

title: Span Subspan
description: Create a sub-view of a span (C++20)
explanation: Subspan creates a non-owning view over a portion of the span.

title: Span As Function Parameter
description: Use span to accept any contiguous container as function parameter (C++20)
explanation: Span works with arrays, vectors, and other contiguous containers.

title: Concept Auto (C++20)
description: Use concepts with auto to constrain template parameters (C++20)
explanation: Concepts constrain template parameters, providing better error messages.

title: Custom Concept (C++20)
description: Define a custom concept using requires clause (C++20)
explanation: Custom concepts specify compile-time constraints on template arguments.

title: Requires Clause (C++20)
description: Use requires keyword to constrain template (C++20)
explanation: Requires clause specifies conditions that template arguments must satisfy.

title: Spaceship Operator (C++20)
description: Default three-way comparison using spaceship operator (C++20)
explanation: Default <=> generates all comparison operators (<, >, <=, >=, ==, !=).

title: Spaceship Manual (C++20)
description: Custom three-way comparison implementation (C++20)
explanation: Manual <=> allows custom ordering logic.

title: Ranges Filter View (C++20)
description: Filter elements using ranges view (C++20)
explanation: Filter view applies a predicate to include only matching elements.

title: Ranges Transform View (C++20)
description: Transform each element using ranges view (C++20)
explanation: Transform view applies a function to each element lazily.

title: Ranges Pipe Composition (C++20)
description: Compose multiple range views with pipe operator (C++20)
explanation: The pipe operator composes views lazily and efficiently.

title: Ranges Sort (C++20)
description: Sort using the ranges algorithm (C++20)
explanation: Ranges::sort sorts in-place just like std::sort but with a simpler interface and projections.

title: Fold Expression Unary (C++17)
description: Apply operator over a parameter pack using unary fold (C++17)
explanation: Fold expressions reduce a parameter pack with a binary operator.

title: Fold Expression Binary (C++17)
description: Apply fold with an initial value (C++17)
explanation: Binary fold uses an initial value, useful when the pack could be empty.

title: If Constexpr (C++17)
description: Conditionally compile code using compile-time if (C++17)
explanation: If constexpr discards the unused branch at compile time, reducing code bloat.

title: Nodiscard Attribute (C++17)
description: Warn when return value is discarded (C++17)
explanation: [[nodiscard]] encourages callers not to ignore the return value.

title: Maybe Unused Attribute (C++17)
description: Suppress unused variable warnings (C++17)
code:
[[maybe_unused]] int debugVar = 42;
[[maybe_unused]] void helper() {}
explanation: [[maybe_unused]] tells the compiler not to warn about unused entities.

title: Fallthrough Attribute (C++17)
description: Indicate intentional fallthrough in switch (C++17)
explanation: [[fallthrough]] documents and suppresses warnings for intentional case fallthrough.

title: Deprecated Attribute (C++14)
description: Mark entities as deprecated (C++14)
code:
[[deprecated("Use newFunction instead")]]
void oldFunction() {}
explanation: Using deprecated entities triggers compiler warnings.

title: Likely Unlikely Attribute (C++20)
description: Hint branch prediction probability (C++20)
explanation: Likely/unlikely hint the optimizer about which branch is more probable.

title: Structured Bindings With Array (C++17)
description: Unpack array elements using structured bindings (C++17)
explanation: Structured bindings decompose arrays into named variables.

title: Structured Bindings Struct (C++17)
description: Unpack struct members using structured bindings (C++17)
explanation: Structured bindings can decompose any aggregate.

title: Structured Bindings With Map Iteration
description: Use structured bindings to iterate over map (C++17)
explanation: Structured bindings make map iteration cleaner and more readable.

title: Template Lambda (C++20)
description: Lambda with explicit template parameters (C++20)
explanation: Template lambdas allow naming template parameters explicitly.

title: Range Based For With Initializer (C++20)
description: Range-based for loop with initializer (C++20)
explanation: The initializer in range-for is evaluated once before the loop begins.

title: To Underlying (C++23)
description: Convert scoped enum to its underlying type (C++23)
explanation: to_underlying is a utility to access a scoped enum's underlying integer value.

title: Stacktrace (C++23)
description: Capture current call stack trace (C++23)
explanation: std::stacktrace provides access to the current call stack for debugging.

title: Std Expected (C++23)
description: Return a value or an error without exceptions (C++23)
explanation: Expected holds either a value or an error, similar to Rust's Result type.

title: Std Mdspan (C++23)
description: Multidimensional array view (C++23)
explanation: Mdspan provides a non-owning view over multidimensional arrays.
